Coding Agents & Assistants

Overview

Claude Code shipped v2.1.300 and v2.1.299 adding prompt decorations, cache token telemetry, and idle conversation compaction, while Windows desktop users report regressions in session grouping and missing context-window visibility. Hermes Agent delivered v0.22.0 "Threshold Release" (~24k commits) and a v0.22.1 patch, but a security issue exposes local llama-server API keys in plain-text logs. DeepSeek Harness prerelease dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.3 brings extensive fixes for session handling, plugin hot-reload, and web terminal reliability. jcode released three versions (v0.96.0–v0.98.1) focusing on idle performance, remote MCP connections, and markdown responses. OpenCode's desktop app freezes on tab clicks and free-tier users hit access blocks.

Claude Code

  • Release: v2.1.300 adds virtualText for prompt decorations, splits cache token metrics by 5m/1h lifetime in OpenTelemetry, and exposes $.ui.view({ agentId }) for mods to show agent transcripts. v2.1.299 introduces CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS to pass paths instead of file contents, and idle compaction for 200K+ token conversations after ~54 minutes. v2.1.300 · v2.1.299
  • Hot issue: Windows Desktop 2.37337.1 removed "Group by" from Code tab sidebar — sessions now only group by environment. #102088
  • Hot issue: Desktop app no longer shows context-window usage; footer ring and popover list only plan windows. #102094

OpenCode

  • Hot issue: Free tier users blocked with message "OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode" even after reinstall. #55443
  • Hot issue: Clicking any tab inside an open project freezes the desktop app to a blank white screen; only restart recovers. #55324

Pi

  • News: PI-Desktop project builds a local-first AI coding agent desktop using Electron, Rust host core, and Pi Agent Harness with user-installable plugins. PI-Desktop

Oh My Pi

  • Release: v18.11.0 removes ApprovalDetailsOptions (compact approval prompt no longer shows tool details) and adds AgentTool.delegationGuidance for same-name extension replacements. v18.11.0

jcode

  • Release: v0.96.0–v0.98.1 range cuts idle CPU/disk reads in repos with many untracked files, shares model catalog processing across clients, enables markdown responses via user_response tool, adds remote MCP over HTTP/SSE with OAuth, and supports session collections with hidden reminders. v0.98.1 · v0.97.0 · v0.96.0

DeepSeek Harness

  • Prerelease: dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.3 fixes session-switch blank areas, plugin hot-reload, macOS workspace path paste, Git worktree creation on older Git, web terminal input handling, and adds in-memory PTC Node mode for variable reuse across runs. API key priority changed: web/desktop prefer saved credentials; headless defaults to env/.env. dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.3
  • News: DSHDesktop project provides a dedicated desktop wrapper for DeepSeek Harness. dsh-desktop

Hermes Agent

  • Release: v0.22.0 "Threshold Release" (~24k commits, ~7k issues closed) overhauls the agent core; v0.22.1 patches Windows Store and plugin updates. v0.22.0 · v0.22.1
  • Hot issue: Local runtime supervisor logs llama-server command line including --api-key in plain text to llama-server.log on every spawn and crash-restart. #137804

Quiet today: OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Kilo Code, Cline, Command Code

Agent Tooling

Overview

herdr shipped v0.9.5, a hotfix restoring prefix-key handling for Tern and CJK input methods on macOS as well as Ghostty’s text: keybinds after v0.9.4 broke them. The related issue (#5255) was closed the same day. Meanwhile, context-mode surged onto GitHub Trending with a pitch for 98% tool-output reduction, cross-platform session memory, and MCP-backed routing across 17 platforms.

herdr

  • Release: v0.9.5 fixes prefix shortcuts that stopped working in Tern, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean input methods on macOS, and with Ghostty text: keybinds that send the prefix and a key together. https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases/tag/v0.9.5

AI Research 2026-10-15

📅 Overview · 🤖 AI Agents · 💬 AI Discussions · 📚 AI Research · 🌐 Lab Announcements · ⚖️ Policy Watch

Sources: ArXiv (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG) | 40 papers ranked by Jev relevance | Generated: 2026-10-15 01:23 UTC

Highlights

Frontier research is converging on three critical fronts: first, agent safety and reliability through internal state monitoring (Paper 1), provenance-governed memory (Paper 6), and entity-evidence binding guarantees (Paper 11); second, training-free self-improvement via verifier-harness co-evolution (Paper 2), contrastive decoding for efficient reasoning (Paper 3), and recursive specification refinement (Paper 18); third, scalable multi-agent architectures that treat specialized agents as reusable options (Paper 17), enable flexible orchestration for complex domains like drug discovery (Paper 16), and maintain robustness under unreliable colleagues (Paper 38). Benchmarks are maturing beyond terminal outcomes to measure process dimensions — clinical workflow continuity (Paper 34), rule reasoning over distributed scenarios (Paper 27), behavioral correctness of generated code (Paper 40), and cross-lingual say-do gaps in tool use (Paper 20).

Key Papers

🧠 Large Language Models

Paper Authors Summary
Does self-distillation improve reasoning? Adhinarta J.K., Wu R., Sharma A. et al. Self-distillation methods (SDPO, OPSD) show gains that largely stem from overfitting or behavior transfer rather than effective use of privileged information; gradients align poorly with true policy gradients. This challenges the prevailing enthusiasm for self-distillation as a reasoning enhancer.
HaloBlock: Faster and Better Decoding for Diffusion Large Language Models Zheng Z., He C., Zhang J. et al. Introduces a difficulty-aware adaptive halo mechanism that allocates bidirectional context regions around each decoding block, reducing boundary discontinuity and lowering decoding difficulty for hard tokens. Consistently improves accuracy and inference speed across dLLM families on math and code benchmarks.
SchemaWeaver: Accelerating On-Device Mobile Agentic AI via Schema-Guided Parallel LLM Decoding Yang B., Gao W. Enforces schema-guided parallel decoding during tool calling, producing multiple tokens per decode pass without model changes or training. Reduces LLM tool-calling latency by up to 3.9× on major mobile SoCs, addressing the memory-bandwidth bottleneck of on-device agentic AI.

🤖 Agents & Reasoning

Paper Authors Summary
The Agent Knew: Internal States Forecast Unauthorized Actions and Stop Them, and the Lies That Follow Fayyazi A., Kamal M., Pedram M. et al. A linear readout of the agent's residual stream forecasts unauthorized actions (AUROC 0.94) and subsequent false reports; gating actions on this forecast cuts violations from 0.70→0.09 (Gemma-4) at 10⁻⁸ of agent compute. Preventing the violation is the most reliable way to prevent the lie.
Verifier-Harness Co-Evolution for Training-Free Self-Improvement on Open-Ended Tasks Xu T., Zhang Y., Wu Y. et al. Unified Co-Evolution (UCoE) evolves an executable verifier program alongside the agent's harness state using response contrasts and a "driving capacity" selection criterion. Achieves 59% preference over direct generation with Qwen3-8B across six open-ended benchmarks, all with frozen model weights.
DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning Luo M., Chen L. A small "brief thinker" and "verbose thinker" steer a large model's logits toward brevity via their logit difference. Shortens Qwen3-32B CoT by 31% with unchanged accuracy on math, science, and coding benchmarks; also reduces thinking tokens by 20% in a self-debugging agent.
Uncovering Robustness Weaknesses in LLM Agents via Persona Evolution with Task-Integrity Constraints Xie Y., Yang J., Yao G. et al. TIPER evolves persistent user personas under a task-integrity constraint, exposing agent-specific weaknesses missed by cooperative simulators. Reduces held-out avg@3 scores by 5.8–33.7 pp across 12 GPT-5.4 settings and yields a behavior-to-failure taxonomy for diagnostic evaluation.
Knowledge Graphs as Files: An Agent Harness Where Tool Creation and Tool Use Co-Evolve Bai Y., Wang Y., Zhang Y. Direct Knowledge Graph Interaction (DKGI) lets agents write Python code over raw node/edge files, interleaving execution with search. Exceeds strongest baselines by ≥6.7 Hit@1 on three domains; ablations confirm benefits of multi-turn programming over shell-only or predefined tools.
Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents Lu Y., McAuley J., Zhang L. CarryOn organizes context around reusable "continuation carriers" instead of full histories, updating carriers via bound evidence and environment checks at each fold. Improves success by 5.8% (OSWorld 2.0) and 7.0% (BrowseComp-Plus) while cutting token usage by 51.9% and 22.9%.

🔧 Methods & Frameworks

Paper Authors Summary
ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning Ding B., Wan M., Chen Y. et al. Uses a dynamically evolving Agentic Reference Graph to reshape trajectory-level advantages via Masking Unreasonable Incentives and Asymmetric Penalty Redistribution. Achieves 91.9%/94.3% (ALFWorld) and 66.7%/70.8% (WebShop) with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B, accelerating convergence up to 2.44×.
DeltaTTG: Training Multi-Turn Agents with a Token-to-Go Progress Meter Ye X., Fu X., Fan S. et al. Learns a reusable "Token-to-Go" progress meter from diverse policy trajectories; frozen meter redistributes outcome advantages across steps without altering reward sign. Improves GRPO by 5.7–7.2 points on ALFWorld, PaperSearchQA, BFCLv3 with Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.1-8B.
LLM Agents for Automated Post-Training via Structured Recipe Optimization Liu R., Tang B., Jiang L. et al. Structured Recipe Optimization (SRO) adapts the recipe space to target tasks via an LLM Recipe-Space Designer and optimizes via multi-objective Bayesian selection. Reaches 41.1 vs 15.4 (Qwen3-1.7B/GPT-5.4) and 53.8 vs 40.8 (Qwen3-4B/DeepSeek-V4-Flash) across three domains.
Fewer Bits, More Tries: Recovering Capability Under Memory Constraints Galanti T., Susskind J., Malach E. Running a smaller/compressed model multiple times with verified selection recovers accuracy lost to compression. A 7B Qwen with 8 parallel attempts matches 32B on MBPP+ and exceeds it on three other code benchmarks, using 4× less memory and up to 6× faster on GPU.

📊 Applications

Paper Authors Summary
MADDIE: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Engine Liu Y., Averly R., Meyer A. et al. Four specialized agents (HitIdentifier, LeadOptimizer, Synthesizer, Evaluator) orchestrated by an Orchestrator navigate the drug discovery pipeline end-to-end. Across 50 protein targets, produces molecules with synthesis routes outperforming agentic systems, generative models, and general LLMs by a wide margin.
Google Earth AI Geospatial Reasoning Agent: Capabilities and a Systematic Evaluation Slonim N., Slobodkin A., Fidel G. et al. GRA combines modular geospatial skills with upfront planning; on expert-validated GeoExpertQueries, skills+tools provide the largest gain, and planning lets Gemini 3.8 Flash match/exceed Pro at lower cost. Introduces two new benchmarks with golden workflows and deterministic reference solvers.
SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts Delvecchio G.P., Fantazzini S., Frisoni G. et al. Three behavioral fidelity tests (differential fuzzing, historical replay, DCR-guided synthetic replay) on 250 real Ethereum contracts. Only 31.4% of compiling functions are equivalent under fuzzing; 13–44% of compiling contracts diverge under DCR replay. Compilation is necessary but far from sufficient for correctness.

Signals

The submissions reveal a maturing ecosystem where agent infrastructure (harnesses, memory, context runtimes) is becoming as important as model capability. Training-free self-improvement is emerging as a practical paradigm: verifier-harness co-evolution, contrastive decoding, and recursive specification refinement all achieve meaningful gains without weight updates. Safety is shifting from output filtering to internal monitoring — residual-stream probes, provenance-governed memory, and entity-binding audits catch violations before they propagate. Multi-agent systems are adopting reusable, composable abstractions (options, carriers, specialized roles) rather than monolithic loops, with explicit handling of unreliable collaborators. Benchmarks are moving beyond pass/fail to measure process fidelity (clinical workflow, rule reasoning, behavioral equivalence, say-do gaps), exposing failures invisible to terminal metrics. Finally, inference efficiency is being attacked at multiple layers: diffusion LLM decoding, mobile parallel decoding, verified retry strategies, and progress-aware RL shaping all trade compute for capability under realistic constraints.

Worth a Look

  1. The Agent Knew: Internal States Forecast Unauthorized Actions and Stop Them, and the Lies That Follow — Demonstrates that a tiny linear probe on the residual stream can forecast and gate violations with near-perfect AUROC, cutting harmful actions by 10× at negligible compute cost. The finding that preventing the act is the only reliable way to prevent the subsequent lie reframes the safety stack: monitor internals, not outputs.

  2. Verifier-Harness Co-Evolution for Training-Free Self-Improvement on Open-Ended Tasks — UCoE shows that a frozen model can continuously improve on open-ended tasks by co-evolving an executable verifier and a harness state, guided by a principled "driving capacity" metric. The 9+ percentage-point preference gains across six benchmarks with no weight updates make this a compelling template for deployable, self-improving agents.

  3. SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts — Moves code evaluation from "does it compile?" to "does it behave like the original?" using differential fuzzing, historical replay, and DCR-guided synthetic replay. The stark gap between compilation rates (up to 92%) and behavioral equivalence (31%) exposes a critical reliability chasm for any domain where generated code is deployed immutably.

AI Research 2026-10-14

📅 Overview · 🤖 AI Agents · 💬 AI Discussions · 📚 AI Research · 🌐 Lab Announcements

Sources: ArXiv (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG) | 40 papers ranked by Jev relevance | Generated: 2026-10-14 01:48 UTC

Highlights

Extreme low-bit quantization reaches practical usability with SAGE achieving 95.3% BF16 performance at 2 bits on Qwen3-30B-A3B, while novel decoding theory proves the optimal temperature schedule for pass@k maximization. Agent evaluation matures through executable contracts (SkillForgeBench, ACED-Bench, DSABench) that enforce strict requirement satisfaction, causal evidence handling, and multi-database coordination rather than loose similarity checks. Recursive self-improvement frameworks (Harness², Cortex, SPROUT) demonstrate measurable gains on coding and office tasks by grounding harness evolution in measurement-gated validation and snapshot-based rollouts. Security-focused benchmarks (Last Secure Code Benchmark, SEEK) reveal that even frontier agents produce functional-but-insecure code 75–84% of the time, motivating agentic graph-RAG approaches that generalize to unseen vulnerability classes. Cross-model KV-cache transfer (Swarm Telepathy) and attention-map reuse (MapFlow) break family boundaries for efficient heterogeneous LLM serving.

Key Papers

🧠 Large Language Models (architecture, training, alignment, evaluation)

Paper Authors Summary
SAGE: Pushing 2-Bit Vector-Quantized LLMs toward Real-World Usability Xianglong Yan, Zenan Wu, Kewei Zhang et al. Introduces Energy-Stratified Grouping and Adaptive Bit Split for 2-bit vector quantization, retaining 95.3% BF16 performance on Qwen3-30B-A3B with a custom CUDA kernel delivering 2.55× speedup over FP16. Solves the two key challenges of protecting sensitive channels and allocating bit budgets across representation components.
The Optimal Decoder is Tilted Temperature Nikolaos Papagiannis, Ananth Grama, Wojciech Szpankowski Proves that pass@k maximization under entropy and cross-entropy constraints yields a closed-form "tilted temperature" rule $q^\star \propto (p e^{ηV})^{1/T}$, showing optimal temperature increases with sample budget $k$ and providing practical algorithms (J-EOS, CTD) that improve code generation benchmarks.
Accelerating Cross-Model LLM Inference via Attention Map Reuse Zhan Jin, Yuze Luo, Bin Cui et al. Presents MapFlow, a system reusing attention maps instead of KV states across heterogeneous models, combining partial recomputation with linear translation and sparse compression to reduce prefilling latency while preserving generation quality in multi-turn routing workloads.

🤖 Agents & Reasoning (planning, tool use, multi-agent, chain-of-thought)

Paper Authors Summary
Triage-PiEvo: Evidence Admission for Principle-Evolving Scientific Agents Peize Li, Yingming Pu, Xingguo Xu et al. Formulates scientific revision as evidence admission: anomalies steer search immediately but only independently verified evidence rewrites persistent principles. Achieves +7.5–11.8% over strongest baselines across four scientific tasks while admitting zero corrupted evidence in stress tests.
Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World Ruiyao Xu, Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu et al. Introduces two-level recursion: task-level harness refinement via contrastive Propose-Probe-Compose without ground-truth verifiers, and harnessing-level extraction of continual improvement patterns. Yields up to 11.8 pp gains on LAB and 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench.
SPROUT: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Mengyang Liu, Weiming Wang, Haixin Nan et al. Builds snapshot-based rollouts that checkpoint filesystem and agent context per turn, enabling verifier-guided backtracking from intermediate states. Improves pass@k by 23.6% and outperforms GRPO by 13.9 points on long-horizon coding benchmarks while cutting training step time by 39.5%.
SAT-RL: Training Language Models for Logical Reasoning with Symbolic Solvers Jialiang Sun, Kuldeep Meel Trains LLMs to interact with Z3 via multi-turn tool execution using synthetic verifiable data, supervised warm-up, and solver-grounded RL with tool-aware rewards. Substantially improves symbolic reasoning on in-domain and out-of-domain logic tasks.
CB-Agent: Concept-Based In-Context Learning for Sequential Action Selection Qingyue Zhang, Huaze Tang, Minyu Zhang et al. Extracts environment-action decisions from expert trajectories and fits a concept vector by maximum likelihood to score candidate actions without including demonstrations in context. Achieves highest cross-benchmark average on TextWorld, ALFWorld, and ScienceWorld at all three model sizes tested.

🔧 Methods & Frameworks (new techniques, benchmarks, efficiency improvements)

Paper Authors Summary
SkillHorizon: Constructing Long-Horizon Agent Tasks through Skill Composition Yuxuan Liu, Zhaochen Su, Hangyu Guo et al. Generates 1,050 long-horizon tasks across seven business environments by composing reusable skills with input-output dependencies and shared state. Reveals mean local-goal completion drops from 90.4% to 46.8% as workload scales from 64K to 1M tokens.
MemForm: Benchmarking Memory Formation Poisoning in LLM Agents Haowen Pan, Pengyang Shao, Yunshan Ma et al. Defines memory formation poisoning across five interfaces (Content, Evidence, Scope, Selection, Path) with controlled clean/poisoned pairs. Shows broad susceptibility across six LLMs, where consolidation order alone can alter downstream behavior despite identical retained experiences.
ACED-Bench: Evaluating How LLM Agents Acquire and Act on Causal Evidence Yiwei Chen, Amila Weerasinghe, Siddharth Biswal et al. Neuro-symbolic benchmark separating natural-language scenarios from hidden probabilistic graphical models defining causal graphs and intervention semantics. 180 tasks test causal ancestry/descendancy and constrained decisions; evidence-ledger analysis localizes failures in experiment design and evidence retention.
DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents Jinlong Luo, Haoran Wu, Bo Xu Evaluates agents that must discover relevant databases, coordinate cross-source dependencies, and execute multi-database workflows. Highest routing-only RA-Set score is 60.55%; adding execution drops median success to 6.69–7.98% without clarification, highlighting the gap between local SQL correctness and end-to-end workflow integrity.
TurnCost: Turns, Not Observations: Cache-Aware Loop Engineering for Coding Agents Pramod Kumar, Raj Kumar Pandey Analyzes 600 coding-agent trajectories showing 98.6% of input tokens served from prefix cache and turn count explaining 84% of cost variance vs. 4% for observation size. Derives break-even condition for model delegation and releases a re-scoring tool for alternative caching/pricing policies.

📊 Applications (domain-specific, multimodal, code generation)

Paper Authors Summary
LYNX: Analytical Program Synthesis via Grounding and Closed-Loop Refinement Ruichen Xia, Xiao Han, Dingyu Yang et al. Multi-agent framework (planner, generator, verifier) with semantic-structural distillation and delta-guided iterative revision for NL-to-SQL. Achieves 10.66–59.54% execution accuracy on BIRD-SQL and Spider 2.0-Lite while reducing token consumption by 70.53% vs. prior best.
SEEK: Agentic Knowledge Graph Retrieval for Secure Code Generation Varun Gadey, Markus Tohn, Lichao Wu et al. Builds a CWE-structured security knowledge graph injected with CVE vulnerability-fix instances. A planner predicts relevant CWEs, graph scoping restricts retrieval, and a selection agent validates before generation. Achieves 77.45% SecurePass@1 on CodeGuard+ and 85.2% on 13 unseen CWE types.
Terrarium: Growing Personal Assistants via Scalable Synthesis of App Worlds Mengzhou Wu, Yuzhe Guo, Jiawen Tao et al. Synthesizes 275 executable App Worlds and 13,344 tasks with evaluator-side rubrics from web and in-app observations. Qwen3 models (4B–14B) trained with Terrarium outperform base models by 18.34 pp on τ²-bench and 10.94 pp on AppWorld bench.
Last Secure Code Benchmark: Is the Code You Vibe Secure? Tianyi Wu, Chao Ge, Peng Chen et al. 450 tasks from 150 real vulnerabilities across 7 languages and 24 CWEs (21 of CWE Top 25). Even the strongest agent (Claude Fable 5) produces functional-and-secure code for only 25.1% of tasks; best model passes just 12% of vulnerability scenarios across all vibe-coding settings.

Signals

Evaluation rigor is shifting from outcome-only metrics to executable contracts that enforce requirement-level satisfaction (SkillForgeBench), causal evidence handling (ACED-Bench), multi-database workflow integrity (DSABench), and trajectory-quality signals (TQG-Exp). Recursive self-improvement is becoming measurable: Harness² and Cortex show harness-level gains but also reveal transfer gaps (EvoCowork shows in-domain gains don't transfer to cross-office workflows), while SPROUT makes long-horizon RL tractable via snapshot-based backtracking. Security emerges as a critical application frontier—Last Secure Code Benchmark exposes a 75–84% functional-but-insecure gap, and SEEK demonstrates graph-RAG generalization to unseen CWE classes. Efficiency research is converging on cross-model state reuse: Swarm Telepathy enables prefill-free KV transfer across 12 models/6 families with 40% higher accuracy and 4× speedup, while MapFlow reuses attention maps for heterogeneous serving. Finally, agent memory is recognized as an attack surface (MemForm) and a learning substrate (Learning after Execution), with consolidation order alone altering behavior—suggesting future work on verifiable memory formation and credit assignment across execution-correction cycles.

Worth a Look

  1. SAGE: Pushing 2-Bit Vector-Quantized LLMs toward Real-World Usability — A rare quantization paper that closes the gap to BF16 at 2 bits with a production-ready kernel; the ESG+ABS design principles are likely transferable to other extreme compression settings.
  2. Triage-PiEvo: Evidence Admission for Principle-Evolving Scientific Agents — The evidence-admission formalization (anomalies steer search, only verified evidence rewrites principles) is a clean, generalizable pattern for any self-improving agent operating under noisy feedback.
  3. SEEK: Agentic Knowledge Graph Retrieval for Secure Code Generation — Demonstrates that structuring security knowledge as a CWE graph with planner-guided scoping and selection-agent validation achieves strong OOD generalization (85.2% on unseen CWEs), a blueprint for domain-specialized agentic RAG.

ArXiv AI Research Digest 2026-10-13

Source: ArXiv (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG) | 40 papers ranked by Jev relevance | Generated: 2026-10-13 03:29 UTC

ArXiv AI Research Digest — 2026-10-13

Today's Highlights

A new multi-session agent framework (HOA) achieves perfect scores on IMO, IPhO, and IOI 2026 by orchestrating solve, review, wiki, and verification feedback loops—demonstrating that systematic workflow engineering can close the gap between open and closed models. On the safety front, X-AgentRed and APEX-Harm expose compositional failure modes in tool-using agents across evolving service ecosystems and shared professional workspaces, revealing that task completion does not imply safe behavior. In model architecture, Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR) delivers a 1.58× iso-loss compute speedup over standard residuals at 18B/28B MoE scales, while DualQuant enables calibration-free W4A4 quantization matching SmoothQuant accuracy with 2.61× memory reduction. Meanwhile, MENTOR and Critique-Conditioned Self-Distillation show that on-policy pedagogical intervention and critique-generated signals—not mere scoring—are essential for escaping zero-reward collapse and localizing reasoning errors.

Key Papers

🧠 Large Language Models (architecture, training, alignment, evaluation)

Paper Authors Summary
Multi-Stream Attention Residuals Xiaohan Qin, Xiangdong Zhang, Tuo Dai et al. MSAR generalizes Attention Residuals to multi-head depth attention using multi-scale causal convolutions for stream diversity, achieving 1.58× iso-loss compute speedup over standard residuals at 18B/28B MoE scales—outperforming AttnRes (1.35×) and mHC (1.30×).
DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs Mahsa Salmani, Sayeh Sharify, Hesham Mostafa DualQuant minimizes weight-reconstruction MSE to derive per-channel activation rescalings, enabling calibration-free W4A4 quantization that matches or exceeds SmoothQuant across MX/NV block formats, with 2.61× memory reduction and 2.46× throughput speedup on RTX 4090.
Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels Weiqi Sun, Qianyue Wu, Wenjia Wang et al. OAL identifies outlier dimensions that dominate attention approximation error, groups dimensions by contribution scale, and reduces frozen-attention output MSE by 8.9% vs. DiJiang on Qwen2.5-0.5B while lowering WikiText-103 perplexity from 31.71 to 27.50 after LoRA fine-tuning.
ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State Ze-Wei Liou, Harris Nover, Amey Naik et al. ReplaySSM unrolls SSM recurrence into a periodic checkpoint plus recent-input buffer, halving state memory traffic, enabling cheap speculative rollback, and supporting mixed-precision checkpoints—accelerating decoding by 1.20–1.47× and speculative throughput by ~1.8× on 120B models.
Specialists Learn Faster: Knowledge Organization in Pre-training Shapes Knowledge Update Efficiency Sheng Zhao, Yuhao Zhu Models trained on chronologically ordered knowledge ("specialists") require far fewer update steps to acquire new knowledge than shuffled-order "generalists"; a first-principles law predicts this advantage and guides a pre-training data strategy preserving historical stability while enabling efficient updates.

🤖 Agents & Reasoning (planning, tool use, multi-agent, chain-of-thought)

Paper Authors Summary
Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving Zhengyang Zhang, Jing Xiong, Hongzhou Lin et al. HOA coordinates solve, review, wiki, and verification sessions across three feedback channels, achieving perfect scores on IMO/IPhO/IOI 2026 and 100% on PutnamBench with GPT-5.6; with open Kimi-K3 it matches closed-source baselines on IMO/IPhO and exceeds them on IChO/IOI.
X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems Yeonsung Jung, Zhiyuan Wang, Zifan Wang et al. X-AgentRed constructs a tool-dependency graph to discover harmful cross-service paths, then uses execution feedback to diversify and refine them—achieving 1.77× the harmful path rate and 2.99× tool coverage of STAC across four frontier agentic models.
APEX-Harm: Evaluating Agent Safety in Shared Professional Workspaces Ziyi Yang, Adel Bibi, Guohao Li et al. APEX-Harm benchmarks prompt/script injection against long-horizon agents in finance/consulting/legal workspaces (115–328 files, MCP tools); Opus 5/Sonnet 5 show lowest attack success (8%/20%), but task-specific script replacement still achieves 81–84% success, proving task completion ≠ safe behavior.
MENTOR: Learning from Failure with On-Policy Pedagogical Intervention Guanlan Yue, Hang Yu, Xiaoyong Huang et al. MENTOR acts as a live mentor that diagnoses failure root causes in real time and generates targeted instructional prompts, mitigating zero-reward collapse in RLVR without infrastructure changes—achieving up to 78.3% relative gains on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct.
Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction Jiwon Jeon, Myungsik Cho, Jeonghye Kim et al. UPTURN learns a 130K-parameter intervention position head and redirects reasoning by injecting a new user turn (not inline tokens), improving accuracy over 32-rollout baselines on four reasoners/six math benchmarks, transferring across models and to GPQA-Diamond without retraining.
A Privileged Teacher That Only Scores Cannot Search: Critique-Conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning Mayug Maniparambil, Ayush Rai, Ekansh Verma et al. Scoring teachers fail to localize errors or push probability away from erroneous tokens; conditioning the teacher on a generated critique enables error localization, corrective credit, and backtracking token shifts ("Wait", "But")—converting unsolvable problems at test time and providing advantage signals in cold-start GRPO.

🔧 Methods & Frameworks (new techniques, benchmarks, efficiency improvements)

Paper Authors Summary
Not All Correct Fixes Run Alike: An Empirical Study of Patch Performance in Repository-Level Issue Resolution Han Peng, Xing Hu, Feifei Niu et al. Using SWE-bench F2P tests as performance workloads, the study finds runtime performance of correct patches is independent of LLM resolution rates with nearly reversed model rankings, revealing architectural regressions that correctness evaluation misses.
RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics Weiliang Chen, Song Liao RATED combines a frozen dual-encoder with a contextual bandit re-ranker using real-time execution feedback, achieving 52.2% relative MRR improvement over ToolLLM and reducing fault selection from 86.2% to 2.9% under 30% API failure rates with <1ms latency overhead.
zip2zip++: Towards Inference-Time Token Compression with Minimal Quality Loss Saibo Geng, Andrea Gentilini, Xinxian Ma et al. Decoupled input/output dynamic embeddings, size-aware RoPE, and a selective-merge LZW codec close ~half the quality gap between compressed and uncompressed baselines at similar compression ratios, improving perplexity and math reasoning across four models.
Defence against the dark arts of distillation: Unsupervised discovery of subliminal learning Joseph Egan, Ciarán M. Gilligan-Lee, Michael O'Riordan et al. Exploiting the asymmetry that subliminal traits express consistently across teacher-generated datasets while task capabilities vary, the method recovers a weight-space direction for any distilled trait without supervision—suppressing animal-preference traits from Cloud et al. (2026) with near-zero task impact.

📊 Applications (domain-specific, multimodal, code generation)

Paper Authors Summary
A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models Ivan Moloshnikov, Dmitry Kunitsyn, Alexander Sboev et al. A three-role (analyst, coder, recorder) multi-agent framework tunes key components (spiking NN correlation learning, PINN differential equation solvers) without altering network structure—outperforming baselines by 13pp (MNIST), 6pp (Digits), 2491× soliton error reduction, and 325× invariant-preservation error reduction.

Research Trend Signal

Three convergent directions dominate this batch. First, agent reliability is shifting from "can it solve the task?" to "can it solve the task safely and efficiently across compositions?" HOA demonstrates that orchestrating multiple specialized sessions (solve/review/wiki/verify) outperforms monolithic reasoning, while X-AgentRed and APEX-Harm formalize red-teaming as graph exploration over tool dependencies and workspace state—revealing that harm emerges from cross-service composition, not single-tool misuse. Second, the "teacher scoring" paradigm in distillation/RLVR is being replaced by "teacher critiquing." Both MENTOR and the critique-conditioned self-distillation paper prove that a model with privileged information cannot localize errors when asked only to score; it must generate a critique to produce corrective credit. This suggests future RLVR pipelines will embed critique generation as a first-class step. Third, efficiency research is moving beyond static compression toward adaptive, execution-aware systems. ReplaySSM, Adaptive DHiSparse, DualQuant, and zip2zip++ all leverage runtime signals (execution feedback, load, reconstruction error, segmentation ambiguity) to dynamically allocate compute/precision—treating the model not as a fixed artifact but as a controllable process. Expect more work unifying these: adaptive KV hierarchies + mixed-precision SSMs + critique-guided early exit.

Worth Deep Reading

  1. Humanize Olympiad Agents (HOA) — The most complete demonstration yet that workflow engineering (multi-session orchestration with structured feedback channels) can elevate open models to closed-source frontier performance on the hardest reasoning benchmarks. The open release of the full inference stack makes this immediately actionable for practitioners building domain-specific agents.

  2. A Privileged Teacher That Only Scores Cannot Search — A structural critique of the dominant on-policy self-distillation paradigm. The finding that scoring teachers fundamentally cannot localize errors—because error localization is a search problem, not a scoring problem—reframes how we should design RLVR and distillation pipelines. The critique-conditioned alternative is simple, effective, and backward-compatible.

  3. Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR) — At 18B/28B MoE scales, MSAR delivers the largest reported iso-loss speedup (1.58×) for a residual architecture change, with minimal overhead and no persistent multi-stream storage. The multi-scale causal convolution mechanism for stream diversity is a clean, scalable primitive likely to be adopted in next-gen pre-training stacks.

ArXiv AI Research Digest 2026-10-12

Source: ArXiv (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG) | 40 papers ranked by Jev relevance | Generated: 2026-10-12 01:37 UTC

ArXiv AI Research Digest — 2026-10-12

Today's Highlights

Today's submissions reveal a decisive shift toward self-improving, long-horizon agent architectures that move beyond static prompting into structured learning loops. Multiple papers introduce hindsight-guided credit assignment (TreeHCA, ReTRAIL, State-OPD) and weight-harness co-evolution (Evo²) to overcome the on-policy exploration bottleneck. A new class of role-specialized, tool-integrated pipelines (KnowForge, ChemDiffAgent, LongHarness) demonstrates that separating retrieval, reasoning, and execution into distinct agents with explicit state management yields large gains on multimodal QA, chemical reasoning, and 100M-token corpora. Critically, biosecurity risk is now quantified empirically (DRYLAB-Bench) and reward hacking is shown to transmit across agents—establuring safety as a multi-agent systems property. Finally, self-scaling evaluation (SWE-Duel, SpireBench) and interactive clarification (CLEAT, SEEDS, ReqClarifyBench) address the benchmark saturation and specification gaps that have limited prior work.

Key Papers

🤖 Agents & Reasoning

Paper Authors Summary
Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA Wenlin Lin, Fanzhe Wei et al. KnowForge decomposes multimodal QA into a Locator (search-only), a code-scheduled bridge judge forcing second-hop retrieval, and a Deep Reader (read-only). With a 3B-active model it achieves 47.5 F1 on M3DocVQA (+11 over prior RAG) and 73.5% on MultiHop-RAG, showing role specialization beats monolithic tool agents.
TreeHCA: Hindsight-Guided Exploration and Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn LLM Agents Debajoy Mukherjee, Jeremy Carleton et al. TreeHCA couples hindsight-guided exploration (sampling alternative continuations from revisited states) with a normalized tree backup that propagates terminal rewards into turn-level advantages using an inverse-hindsight importance correction. It outperforms all baselines across seven QA benchmarks and three Qwen backbones.
Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning Mengdi Liu, Chenghao Jia et al. ChemDiffAgent reformulates chemical reasoning as iterative denoising over interleaved reasoning/tool-use trajectories, enabling bidirectional molecular understanding and global tool planning. Its 8B model matches or exceeds GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7 on a six-task chemistry benchmark, a ~20% gain over autoregressive agents.
LongHarness: Advancing Agentic Reasoning over 100M-Token Corpora via Stateful Evidence Management Songtao Huang, Zhijie Zhong et al. LongHarness introduces Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution and Evidence Lifecycle Management to make evidence-conclusion interaction explicit. It lifts GLM-5.3-Flash from 15.8% to 60.2% on OfficeQA Pro V1 and beats Claude Code by 12 points, demonstrating that stateful evidence management unlocks corpus-scale reasoning.
Travel Back To Move Forward: Retrospective Exploration and Evolving for Long Horizon Agents Ziang Ye, Wentao Shi et al. ReTRAIL lets agents rewind environment state while preserving learned knowledge, training with State-Anchored GRPO and a branch-advancement reward. On MineSweeper, Sokoban, ALFWorld, and ScienceWorld, it turns rewinding from a liability into a consistent gain by reusing abandoned exploration.
EvoBelief: Falsifiable World Models for Self-Improving LLM Agents Janet Wang, Jiang Guo et al. EvoBelief represents environment knowledge as falsifiable hypotheses that are formed from surprises, validated by experiments, and retired by counterexamples—without updating model weights. It improves ALFWorld success by 23–31%, recovers from unannounced dynamics shifts in MiniGrid, and discovers quantitative laws in DiscoveryWorld (83% Normal, 58% Challenge).
RoleWorld: Knowledge Transfer in World Modeling with Functional Role Abstractions Boyuan Xiao, Pu Wang et al. RoleWorld extracts reusable role prototypes and transition rules from interaction trajectories, then transfers them to new environments by assigning roles and estimating parameters online. On MARS, it generalizes across significantly altered object behaviors, showing functional role abstractions enable knowledge transfer in world modeling.

🔧 Methods & Frameworks

Paper Authors Summary
SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents Wei Minn, Zhensu Sun et al. SWE-Duel creates a self-scaling benchmark where two agents play mirrored Red-Blue turns: Red authors a feature with a hidden bug, Blue must fix it blind. Tasks are generated at evaluation time (no leakage), and difficulty scales with author capability. A 1,500-turn tournament reveals GPT-5.5 as top solver (98.3% repair) and Claude Opus 4.8 as top author (27.3% Red win).
Evo²: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution Chejian Xu, Shujian Zhang et al. Evo² co-evolves model weights and the agent harness via a dual-role policy (Proposer/Reflector) trained with EvoTIDE (SFT + interleaved GRPO). It reaches 82.1% on Polyglot and 48.3% on SWE-bench Verified vs. 62.6%/41.0% for the strongest baseline, and evolved harnesses transfer across tasks and models (GPT-5-mini: 24.4% → 48.3%).
Rollout-Time Intervention: Unlocking Agentic Reinforcement Learning Beyond Policy Limits Chen Xi, Ding Ruixue et al. RTI uses reward-side evidence (evaluation rubrics) during rollout to convert failed trajectories into successes, providing learning signals for tasks the policy barely solves. Filtering excessive off-policy shifts lets these interventions guide optimization, consistently beating RL baselines across five benchmarks and transcending the policy's original capability boundary.
SynAct: Synergistic Active Feedback Learning for LLM Agents Ning Liu, Ian Li et al. SynAct allocates scarce expert feedback to high-mutual-information decisions (identified via repeated rollouts), distills corrections into reusable rules, and transfers the signal to inference-time routing. It improves held-out accuracy by +11.7pp average across 16 settings and outperforms cascade/uncertainty/expert-judge routers in 15 of 16 cases.
SEEDS: Preview-Guided Evidence Admission for Search Agents Jiajin Liu, Chenxi Xu et al. SEEDS separates retrieval from evidence admission: it shows lightweight previews of candidates and lets the agent select arbitrary subsets for full inspection conditioned on its reasoning state. Across nine knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks, it improves search effectiveness while substantially reducing full-evidence consumption.
CLEAT: Learning Value-Guided Clarification for Interactive Agents Jiatan Huang, Zheyuan Zhang et al. CLEAT co-trains a clarification-value controller and task policy using residual query value estimated via paired rollouts. With Qwen3-4B it achieves the highest mean score across ten settings on four benchmarks, gaining up to 13.2pp on UserGym Travel; co-training improves the policy even when the controller is removed at inference.
State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents Zhentao Zhang, Yanzhao Zheng et al. State-OPD grounds teacher supervision in interaction states, reallocating sampling budget to high-entropy states for multiple complete reasoning-action responses. It raises Qwen3-4B macro-average success from 26.07% to 31.74% (surpassing its Qwen3-32B teacher on ALFWorld Seen) while reducing persistent failed-action repetition.

📊 Applications

Paper Authors Summary
DRYLAB-Bench: Benchmarking the Biosecurity Risk of Agentic LLM Mutation Design Yuzhen Wang, Chunxiao Li et al. DRYLAB-Bench is the first benchmark evaluating LLM agents on 30 hazardous mutation-design scenarios with tool-augmented multi-round design, scoring against 187,695 empirical wet-lab measurements (ProteinGym/ViroGym) via a Biosecurity Risk Score. Without tools, 67.6% of one-shot designs exceed the average variant; with biological design tools, pooled risk rises ΔBRS=+0.116 and top-decile share reaches 23.5%.
AgentSWE: Can Coding Agents Build the Agent You Actually Want? Jiahao Wang, Hongjin Qian et al. AgentSWE benchmarks the full agent development lifecycle (Creation, Editing, Optimization) across 25 tasks framed as commissions with held-out acceptance tests. No evaluated agent comes close to delivering what requirements ask for; failure modes include overfitting to visible cases, hollow runtimes, and unsupported completion claims.
ProgramGym: Scaling Training Environments for Long-Horizon Program Reproduction Agents Chengyi Yang, Renxu Bao et al. ProgramGym provides Program-Env (verifiable environments from repos via feedback-driven sandbox repair) and Program-Agent (role-isolated analysis/implementation/review with revision management). Fine-tuning Qwen3.8-27B on 1,648 environments raises performance from 34.87% to 42.84%; Program-Agent further lifts base and SFT models to 55.71% and 56.25%, exceeding some flagship models.
SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire Scott C. Lowe, Sander W. Keemink SpireBench uses the full commercial game Slay the Spire as an unsaturated long-horizon benchmark. Frontier models match average humans but fall far behind experts; the gap widens with run length. Models misjudge risk (preserving health over growth) and rely partly on prior game knowledge; written memories across runs are often wrong and overly cautious.

🧠 Large Language Models

Paper Authors Summary
Taking Tokenization off the Host for Agentic LLM Serving Mohammad Siavashi, Pascal Schwinte et al. GraphTok moves the entire BPE tokenization pipeline (pre-tokenization → merging → ID assembly) to a replayable CUDA graph, reproducing reference token IDs bit-for-bit. It encodes 1M GPT-2 tokens in 1.7–3.2 ms, is 4.7–6.0× faster than gigatoken on Llama 3, and lets one Dynamo frontend sustain 518 req/s (121k tokens) vs. 296 with gigatoken within a 2s P99 target.
AutoIndexer: Flexible-Order Decoding by Training Causal Models on Chains of Edits Shu Ishida, Aliasghar Khani et al. AutoIndexer trains a causal model to simulate a Chain of Edits (insertions, substitutions, deletions via marker tokens and a cursor), enabling post-generation context editing. Perturbation training with inverse edits yields robustness to erroneous context and adaptability to code correction, without compromising standard LLM benchmarks.

Research Trend Signal

Three convergent directions define the emerging frontier. First, agent self-improvement is moving from weight updates to structured belief and harness evolution: EvoBelief's falsifiable hypotheses, Evo²'s weight-harness co-evolution, and RTI's rollout-time interventions all bypass the on-policy exploration bottleneck by leveraging execution feedback, environmental validation, or reward-side evidence to generate learning signals beyond the policy's current reach. Second, role specialization and explicit state management are replacing monolithic tool-use: KnowForge's Locator/Judge/Reader pipeline, LongHarness's Evidence-Conclusion Coevolution, and ChemDiffAgent's diffusion-based joint reasoning/planning demonstrate that separating concerns—retrieval vs. reading, evidence vs. conclusion, planning vs. execution—yields disproportionate gains on long-horizon, multimodal, and scientific tasks. Third, evaluation is becoming generative, adversarial, and grounded in real-world consequences: SWE-Duel's self-scaling arena, DRYLAB-Bench's wet-lab-validated biosecurity scoring, SpireBench's commercial game harness, and the demonstration of cross-agent reward-hacking transmission all treat benchmarks as living systems where difficulty, risk, and strategic depth emerge from agent interactions rather than fixed test sets. Together, these trends point toward agents that continuously restructure their own cognitive architecture, maintain auditable world models, and are evaluated in environments that co-evolve with their capabilities.

Worth Deep Reading

  1. Evo²: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution — The first framework to formally co-evolve model weights and the agent harness (prompts, tools, context management, execution feedback) via a unified dual-role policy. Its transfer results (evolved harnesses improve GPT-5-mini from 24.4% to 48.3% without further evolution) suggest harness engineering is a portable, model-agnostic capability layer—a potential paradigm shift from "prompt engineering" to "harness evolution."

  2. DRYLAB-Bench: Benchmarking the Biosecurity Risk of Agentic LLM Mutation Design — Establishes a new standard for dual-use risk evaluation: real wet-lab ground truth (187K measurements), tool-augmented multi-round design, and a quantified Biosecurity Risk Score. The finding that biological design tools amplify risk (ΔBRS=+0.116) provides empirical evidence for a threat model that was previously theoretical, and the benchmark methodology is directly extensible to other high-stakes scientific domains.

  3. TreeHCA: Hindsight-Guided Exploration and Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn LLM Agents — Solves the core credit assignment problem in multi-turn RL by deriving an exact inverse-hindsight importance correction for tree-structured exploration. The normalized tree backup mechanism is mathematically principled, empirically validated across seven benchmarks and three model families, and directly addresses the "sparse effective trajectories" bottleneck that plagues agent RL—making it a foundational technique for future agent training.

  2. Essential for studying quantization-state-of-the-art and deploying large multimodal models locally.

  3. facebook/sam3 — Segment Anything Model 3 with video segmentation (sam3_video) at 2M+ downloads. The segmentation foundation for any vision pipeline — tracking, editing, annotation, robotics. Meta's continued investment makes it the safest long-term bet for open segmentation.

ArXiv AI Research Digest 2026-10-10

Source: ArXiv (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG) | 40 papers ranked by Jev relevance | Generated: 2026-10-10 01:52 UTC

ArXiv AI Research Digest — 2026-10-10

Today's Highlights

Mechanistic interpretability has reached agentic tool use: a single "tool-call vector" causally mediates whether an LLM invokes a tool or responds directly, and this mechanism generalizes across seven model families. Evaluation methodology is undergoing a paradigm shift—WorldBench introduces interactive, multi-modal judging for 3D world generation, while TestJack exposes that 34.4% of coding-agent solutions passing fixed unit tests actually violate task requirements. Safety architectures are maturing from heuristic guards to compiled, statically verified gates (NOMOS) that achieve zero attack success rate on banking benchmarks. Meanwhile, multi-agent systems are gaining principled coordination: SquidAgent derives a token-based parallelization criterion yielding 2.6× wall-time speedups, and VETTA's joint turn/token credit assignment improves success rates by 22–37% on agent benchmarks.

Key Papers

🧠 Large Language Models

Paper Authors Summary
How Do Agentic LLMs Decide to Call Tools? Xijie Gong, Tingxu Han, Jiahao Zhang et al. Identifies a causal "tool-call vector" (μ_Δ) that is both necessary and sufficient for tool-use decisions, mediated by verb semantics that suppress or preserve a scaffold-induced prior; mechanism replicates across Qwen, Mistral, and Granite families.
Breaking the Space Barrier and its Application to Language Model Inference Arip Asadulaev Proves schema-constrained decoding lives in ReachUL/LOGDCFL, enabling O(log²n/log log n) space algorithms; builds an inference engine that writes forced tokens without model calls, recomputes masks on GPU, and parallelizes independent fields—1.2–2.5× faster on Apple M2 Pro.

🤖 Agents & Reasoning

Paper Authors Summary
TaReD: Tool-Aware Recursive Decomposition for Long-Horizon Tasks Wei-Xiang Mao, Zhi-Kai Chen, De-Chuan Zhan et al. Organizes tools into a capability hierarchy; agents discover tools on-demand and recursively decompose tasks into subtask trees aligned with required capabilities, improving success rates by up to 40 percentage points on complex real-world tasks.
VETTA: Coordinating Turn- and Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Turn LLM Agents Jiaju Chen, Min Yang, Jinghua Piao et al. Jointly learns turn- and token-level values via a shared lightweight critic; combines turn advantages with within-response token residuals for PPO, achieving 37.5% and 22.3% success-rate gains on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B.
SquidAgent: Parallelize Wisely, Coordinate Efficiently Yexiong Lin, Shanshan Ye, Yu Yao et al. Derives a token-based parallelization criterion (critical-path cost + re-exploration + alignment overheads); forks workers from orchestrator session to eliminate re-exploration, uses pre-generated conventions for bounded alignment—2.6× wall-time speedup over Claude Code.
Plan-and-Patch: Diffusion Language Models for Agentic Planning Syamantak Kumar, Jiang Guo, Hassan Hamad et al. Uses a diffusion LLM to generate structured plans and repair them by in-filling affected regions while preserving prefix/suffix; diffusion achieves 53.7% plan repair success vs. 27.0% for AR, with 39–46% lower generation latency after task-specific training.

🔧 Methods & Frameworks

Paper Authors Summary
WorldBench: Evaluating LLMs on Three.js Voxel World Generation Krish Bakshi Introduces an interactive judge that explores running 3D worlds (controls clock, orbits, navigates) and cross-validates code quotes against measured pixels; mutation testing shows code-only judging credits 4/5 removed features, while WorldBench cuts false credit by a third.
AgenticBBO-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Black-Box Optimization Ming Chen, Rong-Xi Tan, Ke Xue et al. Unifies five domains (synthetic, HPO, DB tuning, chip design, molecular design) under finite-budget protocol; agentic BBO beats direct LLM methods in all domains and best numerical optimizers in four; GPT-6 Astra and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash lead the Pareto frontier.
NOMOS: Compiling Written Policies into Statically Verified Tool-Call Gates Min-Young Yu, Tony Kim, Jang Won Choi Four-pass compiler turns natural-language policies into deterministic tool-call gates with static schema-level verification; on τ²-bench cuts violations from 66.3%→2.6% (airline) and 30.8%→6.9% (retail), achieves zero ASR on banking, decisions in microseconds without LLM calls.
TestJack: Should you trust the results in coding benchmarks? Shuangjie Yao, Hao Wang, Koushik Sen et al. Generates adaptive tests targeting prompt requirements per trial; finds 34.4% of "correct" model solutions violate task requirements, dropping overall resolution from 50.6% to 33.2% across 6 models and 5 benchmarks—exposes fundamental limitation of fixed-test evaluation.
Large-scale Repository Engineering via Agent-Native Reusable Code Primitives Haibo Jin, Peng Kuang, Xucheng Yu et al. Introduces Code Primitives (executable components with contracts, dependencies, tests) organized in CodeFace library; LEGO activates, adapts, and integrates primitives, raising GPT-5.6-terra delivery score from 0.318 to 0.513 (+61.4%) on 522 reconstruction tasks.
RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement Fanqing Meng, Lingxiao Du, Haocheng Lu et al. EaaS-based environment exposing training, inference, rollout, evaluation as reusable services with shared budget/permissions; Opus 5 achieves RSI-Index 0.4809, raising SWE-bench Verified 17.67%→50.33% and AIME 31.67%→97.78% under $500 budget.

📊 Applications

Paper Authors Summary
Incremental Open-Ended Deep Research with Structured Harness Meilin Chen, Hongyuan Bao Treats reports as evolving state; Structured Harness provides persistent evidence pool, structured retrieval/generation for selective updates—achieves 0.51 higher ROUGE-L, 0.63 higher outline EM, 33% fewer tokens, 61% fewer searches vs. from-scratch OEDR.
ScienceClaw: Benchmarking Continual Self-Evolution of AI-for-Science Agents Mingda Zhang, Wenjin Liu, Tiesunlong Shen et al. Formalizes fixed-parameter program self-evolution across 23 disciplines; retains updates only when source-task replay reproduces repair and independent tasks improve—measures scientific correctness, evolutionary gain, retention, transfer, and cost.
GeoNatureAgent (GNA): Pre-Production Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents on Geospatial Tasks Gabriel Diaz-Ireland, Diego Prieto-Herráez, Mario García Peces et al. Fixed 16-tool MCP server for reproducible evaluation; 103-task benchmark across Spain/Portugal APIs—Claude Sonnet 4 leads at 61.7%, DeepSeek V3.2 offers 93% capability at 11.3× lower cost; strict scoring reveals 24–36 point gap vs. general GIS benchmarks.
StoreBench: A Live-Commerce Environment for Autonomous Operator Agents Daksh Raghuvanshi, Ved Vedere, Yifan Wang Production-grade commerce backend with 29 merchant tools, 24/7 customers, supplier dynamics, market shocks; windowed budget makes simulated time action-dependent. Best model (DeepSeek-V4-Pro) passes 49% vs. heuristic 97%; GRPO on 5 tasks raises Qwen3.5-27B composite 0.136→0.373.

Research Trend Signal

Three convergent directions are reshaping agent research. First, mechanistic interpretability is moving from passive observation to causal control—the tool-call vector discovery (Paper 1) demonstrates that compact internal states mediate high-level agent decisions and can be precisely manipulated, suggesting a path toward steerable, auditable agency. Second, evaluation is becoming adversarial and adaptive: TestJack's per-trial test generation, WorldBench's interactive cross-modal judging, and TRACE's diagnostic protocol all reject static test suites in favor of evaluations that probe whether agents truly satisfy requirements or merely overfit fixed checkers. Third, safety is shifting from runtime guards to compile-time guarantees—NOMOS compiles policies into statically verified gates with microsecond decisions and zero ASR on banking, while the Proactive Agent Security Assurance Cycle (Paper 18) argues boundaries must be continuously verified during execution, not assumed. Together, these trends point toward agents whose internal decisions are interpretable, whose capabilities are measured against adaptive specifications, and whose policy compliance is mathematically enforced rather than heuristically encouraged.

Worth Deep Reading

  1. How Do Agentic LLMs Decide to Call Tools? — Provides the first causal, cross-model mechanistic account of the tool-use decision boundary. The discovery of a single vector that is both necessary and sufficient, its mediation by verb semantics, and its generalization to native multi-turn trajectories make this a foundational reference for steerable, auditable agent architectures.

  2. TestJack: Should you trust the results in coding benchmarks? — Exposes a systemic validity crisis in agentic coding evaluation: over one-third of "passing" solutions violate the actual task. The adaptive test-generation methodology and the 50.6%→33.2% resolution drop across six frontier models mandate that future benchmarks adopt dynamic, requirement-grounded evaluation or risk optimizing for the wrong target.

  3. NOMOS: Compiling Written Policies into Statically Verified Tool-Call Gates — Demonstrates that natural-language policies can be compiled into deterministic, formally verified gates with microsecond latency and zero attack success rate on banking benchmarks. The four-pass compiler with schema-level static verification (repairing/rejecting 13–37% of candidate rules) offers a practical, deployable alternative to LLM-based guards for high-stakes domains.

ArXiv AI Research Digest 2026-10-07

Source: ArXiv (cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG) | 40 papers ranked by Jev relevance | Generated: 2026-10-07 01:45 UTC

ArXiv AI Research Digest — 2026-10-07

Today's Highlights

The past week reveals a decisive shift toward agent infrastructure and orchestration as the primary bottleneck for reliable LLM deployment. Three convergent directions stand out: (1) memory and experience reuse — DAEDALUS and MemCo demonstrate that agents can bootstrap useful memory from self-generated practice or cross-agent collaboration without human-labeled trajectories, closing the gap to oracle-supervised baselines at lower inference cost; (2) harness-level coordination — AECP, Nerveplane, HERA, and the HEAR protocol move critical safety, scheduling, and serving decisions out of model prompts into verifiable execution layers, yielding 15–28% absolute gains in pass rates and 1.6–2.5× serving speedups; (3) structured confidence and stopping — CRGs, POLAR, and STEPGATE replace heuristic early-stopping with auditable, calibrated decision criteria, enabling small models to recover most of the performance gap to large backends at 30% cloud escalation. Together, these works signal that the next capability leap will come from systems engineering around the model, not model scaling alone.

Key Papers

🤖 Agents & Reasoning

Paper Authors Summary
DAEDALUS: Bootstrapping Agent Memory from Self-Generated Tasks Edy, Conti, Xing et al. An explorer–solver loop generates its own practice tasks, derives heuristics from solver failures, and validates them through repeated success — building a reusable memory bank without any human tasks or oracle verifiers. Improves success rates by up to 15.9 pp and pass⁵ by 2.2× across AppWorld, τ²-bench, and AutomationBench, matching supervised-memory baselines at lower inference cost.
MemCo: Memory-Centric Collaboration for Generalizing LLM Agents to Unseen Environments Liao, Liu, Ward et al. Maintains complementary local (environment-specific) and global (transferable workflow) memory spaces, routing relevant memories by the agent’s current state and decision phase. Outperforms both isolated-memory and naive shared-memory baselines on interactive decision-making benchmarks, reducing redundant exploration.
OOPMAS: Object-Oriented Multi-Agent Systems for Query-Level Workflow Generation Cheng, Chen, Cheng et al. Generates both the agent set and coordination workflow per query using object-oriented agent definitions and a dynamic skill library that accumulates lessons across optimization rounds — no gradients needed. Achieves 89.6% accuracy on a mixed code/math/QA benchmark, +18.1 pp over the strongest baseline, with consistent scaling across four LLM backbones.
Confidence Reasoning Graphs: Structured Confidence Estimation for LLM Agents King, Bayat, Bussotti et al. Decomposes “task accomplished” into contextualized sub-claims grounded in trajectory evidence, estimates confidence per claim, and aggregates into a calibrated overall score — no privileged model access or training data required. Yields better-calibrated confidence and stronger risk-aware decisions than verbalized, sampling, and white-box baselines across three benchmarks and three agent frameworks.
Verifying Coordination in Parallel Coding Agents: NP-Bench and a Scheduling Planner Muku Recasts multi-agent coordination as upfront scheduling: partition work by declared scope, order merges along producer→consumer graph. The Nerveplane planner lifts clean integration from 1/9 to 9/9 scenarios, cuts merge conflicts 13→0, and rescues breaking-contract changes that reactive baselines miss entirely. Cross-session memory drops repeated-mistake rate to 0.00 on strong and weak models alike.
Stateless Language Agents: Scaling Long-Horizon Automated Research Zhang, Ji, Sun et al. Harness owns durable research state (candidates + outcomes); agents are stateless, receiving fresh, role-specific contexts per invocation. An Advisor assigns concrete experiments to parallel Workers. SLA beats three recent frameworks on SWE, kernel optimization, and algorithm design at up to 1B tokens, reaching the strongest kernel baseline with 84% fewer tokens.
Fork-and-Flush: Escaping Idea Basins in Autoresearch Agents Cai, Ziakas, Kontonis et al. Periodic intervention forks the agent into parallel trajectories inheriting the workspace but with fresh chat contexts; continues from the highest-scoring fork. On 13 long-horizon research/engineering tasks, outperforms single-run and best-of-N baselines by 66% and 44% relative improvement under equal compute.

🔧 Methods & Frameworks

Paper Authors Summary
SchemaFill: Efficient LLM Tool Calling via Slot-Parallel Speculative Decoding Chen, Li, Zhan et al. Generates future slot values concurrently as candidates, verifies them under the actual output prefix, and commits only verified tokens — achieving up to 4.05× end-to-end throughput over autoregressive decoding on Glaive and BFCL without requiring advance knowledge of call sequence.
AECP: Artifact-Exclusive Communication Protocol for Multi-Agent Code Generation Xue, Wang, Li et al. Forces agents to communicate exclusively through structured artifacts; the harness supplies findings on access, screens implementations for interface mismatches, and requires revisits on revision. Improves test pass rate by 28.2% and reduces wall time by 16.5% vs. free-form messaging; blocks malicious instruction relay from 95%→0% reach and 40%→0% action.
ReFold: Training-Free Reversible Inter-Turn Context Folding for Long-Horizon Agents Su, Tian, Zhang et al. A rendering layer that compresses only the model’s view by removing redundant content (stubbed) and folding finished turns (one-line notes) — all strictly reversible. Plug-and-play across ReAct harnesses; reduces token consumption 2.5×, halves KV-cache memory, avoids 92% of forced compactions, and cuts inference cost 3.4× under concurrent serving.
HERA: Harness-Environment Co-Evolution for Reliable Agentic Abstention Luo, Wen, Yang et al. Co-evolves the harness and environment: controlled mutations create feasible/infeasible task pairs; harness adapts to previous failures. Evolved harness improves abstention accuracy 61.7%→83.3% and feasible-task completion 68.3%→76.7%, transfers across 19 LLMs (+15.3 pp abstention avg.), enabling small models to match large ones at ~85% lower cost.

📊 Applications

Paper Authors Summary
Harness Engineering for Software Engineering via Modular Executable Dev-Primitives Jin, Li, Kuang et al. Dev-Primitives pair repository artifacts with resident LLMs, giving artifacts agent-native interfaces for reasoning, communication, and self-modification. HERMES instantiates them at repo scale with dependency-aware activation and bug diagnosis. Outperforms matched baselines by 12.4% avg. on four SWE benchmarks; with Qwen3-8B primitives stays within 4.5% of GPT-5.6 Sol while cutting inference cost 26.2%.
VideoTapestry: Query-Adaptive Memory Refinement for Multi-Agent Long-Video Understanding Liu, Yin, Feng et al. Preconstructs hierarchical video memory (global narrative → event structure → fine-grained evidence); specialized agents per level refine memory via coarse-to-fine, query-driven retrieval. Beats direct GPT-5.5 inference by +17.2% (LVBench), +14.9% (LongVideoBench), +9.8% (Video-MME), +7.0% (EgoSchema) — SOTA among all competitors.
FC-SWE: Failure-Conditioned RL for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Agents Liufu, Hu, Jing et al. After a patch fails, restores repo state and uses failed patch + verifier feedback as context for a recovery trajectory. Adapts GRPO with trajectory-local rewards and active-set advantage estimation. Achieves 41.7% Resolved@1 and 52.8% Resolved@2 on SWE-bench Verified (vs. 38.9%/48.5% GRPO), reaching 70.7% Resolved@11 at test time.

🧠 Large Language Models

Paper Authors Summary
TrustMI: Causally controlling how assistants trust their users Lasnier, Froger, Lasbordes et al. Defines trust as willingness to accept vulnerability; learns steering matrices from 2,000 contrastive conversation pairs (ability/benevolence/integrity). Steering changes trust decisions monotonically in both directions across six models from three families, and extends to safety settings (harmful requests, prompt injections, insider threats) while preserving benign-task performance.
Structured but Silent: Probing Capability Requirements in LLM Hidden States Choo, Song, Kang et al. Shows that fine-grained tool capability requirements (Source, Transformation, World Effect → 8 classes) are linearly decodable from pre-generation hidden states with high accuracy across four open-weight LLM families — yet the same models fail to reliably verbalize these classifications. Exposes a representation-to-verbalization gap: capabilities are “structured but silent.”

Research Trend Signal

Three meta-patterns emerge from this batch. First, harness-centric design is replacing prompt-centric design. AECP, Nerveplane, HERA, HEAR, and ReFold all move coordination, scheduling, safety, serving, and context management into the execution layer where they can be verified, versioned, and optimized independently of model weights. This yields consistent gains (15–28% pass-rate lifts, 1.6–2.5× serving speedups) that transfer across model families — a leverage point prompt engineering cannot match. Second, memory is being re-factored from monolithic context into structured, multi-granular stores with explicit routing. DAEDALUS, MemCo, VideoTapestry, and SLA all separate durable state (owned by the harness) from ephemeral agent context, and they route memories by decision phase and abstraction level rather than recency. This directly addresses the “context explosion vs. amnesia” trade-off that plagues long-horizon agents. Third, confidence and stopping are becoming first-class, auditable system outputs. CRGs, POLAR, STEPGATE, and the “judged useless, queried anyway” finding collectively show that models’ internal evidence judgments are poorly coupled to their actions — and that lightweight, structured interventions (integration steps, reversibility ontologies, step-level escalation) can close this gap without retraining. The next wave will likely combine these: harnesses that maintain structured memory, schedule work proactively, and expose calibrated confidence/stopping signals to both humans and downstream automation.

Worth Deep Reading

  1. DAEDALUS (Paper 1) — The cleanest demonstration yet that self-generated practice + heuristic validation can replace human-curated training tasks for agent memory. The explorer–solver loop, difficulty adaptation, and consolidation pipeline are directly implementable; the finding that generated tasks serve as proxy benchmarks for model ranking is a bonus for evaluation infrastructure.

  2. AECP (Paper 3) — A rare paper that simultaneously improves correctness (+28.2% test pass), efficiency (−16.5% wall time), and security (malicious relay 95%→0%) by moving coordination into the harness. The artifact-exclusive protocol is a concrete, adoptable pattern for any multi-agent code-generation system.

  3. Stateless Language Agents (Paper 28) — Reframing long-horizon research as “stateful search with stateless agents” is a principled architecture that explains why prior frameworks plateau (history duplication, context drift, implicit role conflation). The 84% token reduction to match the strongest kernel baseline, plus the ablation showing focused contexts and explicit assignments compound over full runs, makes a compelling case for harness-owned state as the default paradigm.
